articles.title: El Málaga, la defensa donde se acaba la sequía rival
articles.standfirst: Varios delanteros han roto su mala racha contra los blanquiazules
articles.summary: Varios delanteros han roto su mala racha contra los blanquiazules
articles.body: El Málaga CF se ha convertido en las últimas jornadas en un inesperado punto de inflexión para varios delanteros que atravesaban prolongadas sequías goleadoras. Hasta cuatro atacantes han encontrado el camino del gol frente al conjunto de Funes. El caso más reciente se vivió el domingo en La Rosaleda. Mikel Oyarzabal llevaba 13 partidos sin marcar con la Real Sociedad y no encontraba portería desde el pasado 9 de mayo, cuando anotó ante el Real Betis. Su visita a Martiricos, además, estuvo acompañada de un homenaje por su condición de campeón del mundo con España. Después llegó su respuesta sobre el césped: dos goles en pocos minutos y el reconocimiento como MVP del encuentro. Pero Oyarzabal no fue el único jugador de la Real Sociedad que puso fin a una sequía ante el Málaga. Take Kubo también estrenó su cuenta goleadora de la temporada en La Rosaleda. El japonés, con menos protagonismo del habitual durante este curso, aprovechó su oportunidad como titular y tardó apenas tres minutos en marcar. Recibió, trazó su habitual diagonal hacia dentro y disparó desde el vértice del área. El balón, desviado por Pablo Martínez, terminó en la portería. Era su primer tanto con el conjunto donostiarra en 2026 y llegaba después de casi diez meses sin marcar. Su anterior gol había sido el 20 de diciembre ante el Levante. En este periodo, además, una lesión muscular le obligó a permanecer cerca de dos meses apartado. La tendencia ya se había visto una jornada antes. Bryan Zaragoza puso fin ante el Málaga a una racha de más de nueve meses sin marcar y lo hizo estrenándose como goleador con el RCD Espanyol. El extremo no había conseguido marcar durante su etapa en la Roma y su anterior tanto se remontaba al 18 de enero, cuando anotó en el 3-0 del Celta al Rayo Vallecano. Su sequía terminó frente al equipo malaguista, en un encuentro marcado también por la polémica celebración del futbolista. Y la lista tiene un último protagonista. Iván Azón fue el encargado de decidir el duelo entre Getafe y Málaga en el Coliseum. El delantero aragonés apareció en el tramo final para marcar el único tanto del partido y acabar con una racha de diez encuentros oficiales sin encontrar portería. Además, el gol tuvo un significado añadido: supuso su estreno goleador con la camiseta del Getafe, dirigido por José Bordalás. Cuatro atacantes, cuatro sequías y un mismo denominador común: el Málaga ha aparecido en el camino de varios delanteros necesitados de reencontrarse con el gol.

articles.standfirst: Héctor Fort y Aihen Muñoz disputaron el domingo su primer partido como titulares en LaLiga y cumplieron, sumándose como opciones a las rotaciones habituales de Matarazzo
articles.summary: Héctor Fort y Aihen Muñoz disputaron el domingo su primer partido como titulares en LaLiga y cumplieron, sumándose como opciones a las rotaciones habituales de Matarazzo
articles.body: Héctor Fort y Aihen Muñoz disputaron el domingo en La Rosaleda su primer partido como titulares en LaLiga y cumplieron, sumándose como opciones a las rotaciones habituales de Pellegrino Matarazzo, que no estaba echando apenas mano de ellos en los primeros dos meses de temporada. El catalán puede seguir aprovechando la baja por lesión de Jon Mikel Aramburu en el lateral derecho y el canterano darle más respiros que hasta ahora a Sergio Gómez en el izquierdo. Aihen comenzó esta temporada después de haber estado en peligro durante el verano, tras el regreso de Javi López tras su cesión al Oviedo, los rumores sobre el posible interés en fichar un futbolista para esa posición y la posibilidad de subir a Jon Balda, uno de los destacados del Sanse, pero finalmente el ex del Deportivo Alavés volvió a salir a préstamo, no llegó nadie y el canterano continúa en el segundo equipo para recuperar su gran nivel después del problema físico que tuvo al final del pasado curso. El de Etxauri rindió a buen nivel en los amistosos que le tocó jugar en verano y al final formó parte de la plantilla, aunque en los dos primeros meses Matarazzo ha dado total continuidad a Sergio Gómez, hasta que en Málaga decidió darle un descanso. El 3 cumplió y volvió a demostrar que se puede contar con él. Fort, por su parte, aterrizó en San Sebastián a últimos de agosto, después de que la Real decidirá bajar de nuevo a Iñaki Rupérez al Sanse, con un motivo parecido al de Balda, ya que el defensa diestro se pasó toda la pasada temporada en blanco por una lesión que tuvo justo antes del inicio y que le dio varias complicaciones. El jugador formado en La Masía debutó en los últimos minutos del encuentro en Elche, su anterior casa, y tuvo su primera aparición como titular con la elástica txuriurdin en la jornada inaugural de la Europa League frente al Bournemouth, con una mala actuación, por lo que fue sustituido al descanso. Matarazzo ha gestionado luego bien su vuelta al primer plano, que fue un mes después en Málaga, donde cumplió, con la idea de que su rendimiento vaya a más según tenga partidos.

articles.title: Casi 8.000 grupos y 30.000 aficionados han dado el paso para estar en el Nou Mestalla
articles.standfirst: El tamaño medio de los grupos creados hasta la fecha es de 3,67 personas y el plazo se cierra en 30 de octubre
articles.summary: El tamaño medio de los grupos creados hasta la fecha es de 3,67 personas y el plazo se cierra en 30 de octubre
articles.body: El nuevo Mestalla avanza y con él, la mudanza hacia la nueva grada tras más de cien años en la Avenida Suecia es un hecho. El club puso en marcha la pasada semana, el día 14 de octubre, la creación de grupos para ir organizando el traslado con los nuevos pases, los nuevos precios y las nuevas ubicaciones. De momento y hasta el 30 de octubre, fecha en la que se cierra el plazo, el ritmo de grupos es más que satisfactorio. En solo seis días se han creado un total de 7.917 grupos, de los cuales 771 son individuales. La media de personas agrupadas es de 3,67 por unidad por lo que a día de hoy algo menos de 30.000 socios o abonados han dado ya el paso previo para sacar su plaza en el nuevo estadio. Faltan aún diez días para que se cierre el plazo establecido y da la sensación de que el club podrá llegar al tope de 50.000 abonados que se propuso cuando presentó la campaña de traslado. Tras la primera fase y la obtención de un número en la lista de espera por parte de los diferentes grupos, se activará la venta definitiva de los nuevos abonos por orden establecida merced a la antigüedad que se haya calculado en cada grupo. Hay que recordar que pese a los más de 70.000 asientos de los que gozará el Nou Mestalla, el club solo tiene previsto abonar 50.000 para dejar las zonas exigidas por UEFA y en caso de volver a Europa no tener que desplazar a los socios de sus nuevas ubicaciones.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Odds and Rankings after Week 7
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith remains the front-runner for the 2026 Heisman Trophy, but a setback out of his control has created a theoretical twist.
articles.body:
Jeremiah Smith remains the front-runner for the 2026 Heisman Trophy, but a setback out of his control has created a theoretical twist.

During a dramatic win over Indiana, Ohio State saw quarterback Julian Sayin exit with a shoulder injury. He's expected to miss several weeks, handing the keys to the OSU offense to true freshman Luke Fahey.

It's only reasonable to wonder how it might affect the Heisman race.

Throw in the sweeping impact of an upset-riddled Week 7. There's a much different feel to the chasing group as well.

While the latest FanDuel odds are listed, the rankings are more subjective as a snapshot of this moment in the season.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State (+8000)

Conner Weigman, QB, Houston : Weigman racked up 395 total yards and five touchdowns in a valuable win over Oklahoma State. He's at exactly 2,000 offensive yards and responsible for 26 scores at Houston, which is 6-1 and set to play 10th-ranked Utah in a critical Big 12 matchup this weekend.

Kenny Minchey, QB, Kentucky : Although his numbers aren't quite as impressive, Minchey has led Kentucky to a surprising 6-1 start. Still, he's thrown for 1,552 yards with 13 touchdowns to a lone interception. The program's surge is likely to continue as it takes on a 3-4 Vanderbilt next.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State : Despite the tight loss at Houston, Mestemaker hit 300 passing yards for the fifth consecutive game. His margin for error is thinning with OSU at 4-2, but Mestemaker's production—2,082 yards and 18 touchdowns—is keeping him on the fringe of the discussion. Oklahoma State hosts a 2-4 Colorado team in Week 8.

Devon Dampier, QB, Utah : Dampier just navigated a shaky trip to that Colorado squad, throwing for 278 yards and three touchdowns but tossing a pair of interceptions as well. Utah survived and enters a difficult second half of the campaign, starting with a visit from Weigman and Houston.

Gio Lopez, QB, Wake Forest : A newcomer to the watch, Lopez has passed for 1,947 yards with 17 scores to one interception while rushing for 253 yards and six touchdowns. Wake Forest is also 6-1, having fallen only to top-ranked Miami. Following an open weekend, the spotlight will be a little brighter on Lopez.

Bear Bachmeier, QB, BYU : In the upset of Notre Dame, Bachmeier landed his marquee performance. He threw for 224 yards, rushed for 45 yards and caught a 15-yard touchdown, totaling four scores to lead BYU to 6-0. Although his box-score numbers lag behind other top candidates, Bachmeier's peripherals fit a traditional contender. BYU travels to UCF in Week 8.

Gunner Stockton, QB, Georgia : Stockton had a bad game at a rough moment, committing three turnovers in a stunning loss to Auburn. The sky isn't falling, though, since Stockton has 1,730 yards and 17 touchdowns for 6-1 Georgia. Yet after an idle weekend, the schedule only gets tougher.

Josh Hoover, QB, Indiana : What a difference one play makes. Instead of being praised for a last-second touchdown pass to clip Ohio State, Hoover is facing an uphill climb in the Heisman race. If only Nick Marsh's toe hit in-bounds. Nevertheless, as with Stockton, we shouldn't overreact—Hoover has passed for 1,660 yards with 18 scores and zero interceptions. Indiana plays at Michigan next.

CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame : Continue the trend here as Carr handles the aftermath of a disappointing loss at BYU. Notre Dame is still 6-1 entering an idle Saturday, and Carr has thrown for 1,721 yards and 19 touchdowns, with one interception.

Jayden Maiava, QB, USC : Maiava is coming off an open weekend with 2,045 passing yards and 20 total scores on his résumé. USC heads to Wisconsin this weekend before hosting Ohio State.

Latest Report Card Grades for Top 20 CFB QBs

Jesse Legree has steadily risen from a fun, early breakout player to a definite All-American candidate to a legitimate threat for Heisman Trophy votes.

Oregon State has rattled off a 5-2 start, powered by Legree's consistent impact, who's reached the 100-yard mark and scored a touchdown in every game. He's reeled in 46 passes and leads the entire Football Bowl Subdivision in both receiving yards (1,040) and touchdowns (14).

Trips to Fresno State and Boise State remain on OSU's docket, but Legree has a real opportunity to crash the Heisman party.

Overall, it was an ugly evening for Miami. Even as rivalries get weird sometimes, the 'Canes found themselves in a shocking hole at home against Florida State and barely pulled out a double-overtime win.

But the star of the show, yet again, was Malachi Toney.

The sophomore caught 11 passes for 154 yards and two touchdowns, including the game-winner. He also scampered for 31 yards and executed a trick play for a two-point conversion, tossing a pass to Cooper Barkate.

Toney played an absolutely critical role in the 'Canes staying off Saturday's extensive list of highly ranked upsets.

While an outlier performance can happen, we have a solid idea of what Trinidad Chambliss will provide. He'll throw for 200-some yards, make an impact on the ground, account for two-plus scores and push Ole Miss north of 30 points.

Last weekend, he passed for 241 yards and three touchdowns, rushed for a fourth score and propelled the Rebels to a 31-3 victory over Missouri.

The prime-time stage awaits in Week 8 as Ole Miss travels to Texas—which is reeling offensively yet ranks second nationally at 4.2 yards allowed per snap.

Some cracks are beginning to show in the Miami offense. Darian Mensah isn't immune to the side-eyes. He also threw a particularly ugly interception—his first of the year—in the nerve-wracking night against FSU.

He connected on several key passes to help the 'Canes claw back, take a fourth-quarter lead and eventually win 43-35 in overtime. Mensah finished 23-of-34 for 326 yards and three touchdowns.

Miami, newly crowned as the No. 1 team in the nation, carries a 6-0 record into a home matchup with Pitt on Saturday afternoon.

We know Jeremiah Smith is ridiculously talented.

We know he stands atop the FBS with 52 receptions, while ranking second in receiving yards (984) and touchdowns (12).

We know the Buckeyes are dealing with an unexpected dose of adversity, too. As a shoulder injury puts QB Julian Sayin on the shelf for several weeks , OSU is expected to start true freshman Luke Fahey.

Together, can they excel immediately? We don't know. Nobody does.

If there's a bright side to this negative situation, the Bucks have an extra week to prepare for a journey to USC. "Extra work" will undoubtedly be the norm for Fahey and Smith as they attempt to build a rapid connection.

The results will be on full display soon—and impact everything from Smith's award candidacy to 6-1 Ohio State's place in the national hierarchy.

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez: Nicky Butt delivers brutal verdict on Man United star
articles.summary: Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt has reignited his long-standing feud with Lisandro Martinez. The ex-England international famously had a war o...
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt has reignited his long-standing feud with Lisandro Martinez. The ex-England international famously had a war of words with the Argentine defender last season after criticising him ahead of the January Manchester derby.

Martinez, though, managed to prove Butt and United legend Paul Scholes wrong, helping the Red Devils win 2-0 before hitting back at the duo . The 28-year-old was outstanding for the Premier League giants in the second half of last season, helping them finish third in the league.

He carried that form into the 2026 FIFA World Cup, helping Argentina reach the final. Unfortunately, Martinez picked up an injury against Spain and La Albiceleste lost the game.

While the former Ajax defender has recovered over the summer, he has not been at his best this season and has become embroiled in further controversy.

Martinez's open criticism of Jason Wilcox

Martinez has started nine games in all competitions this season and United have won only two of them. The Red Devils have managed just one clean sheet in all competitions, further highlighting the poor state of their backline.

The Argentine defender has scored a goal but has struggled to impress, and has committed one error leading to a goal in the Premier League this season.

Martinez was recently in the news after giving an explosive interview following the 1-1 draw against Atletico Madrid, where he questioned the lack of squad reinforcements. The incident sparked a mixed reaction from fans and pundits, with Wayne Rooney also criticising the Argentine for the outburst.

Martinez, however, retained his place in the starting XI against Leeds United last weekend. His team were leading 1-0 at the break when he had to be taken off due to a knock.

Unfortunately, the Red Devils conceded six minutes into the second half and dropped points once again. While the spotlight remains on Martinez, whose contract expires at the end of this season, Butt has offered his opinion on the player.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast, Butt cited the example of United legend Roy Keane to suggest that a player should only criticise the hierarchy if they can follow it up on the pitch. He said: "You don't come out and speak about the hierarchy like that."

"If you do, you've got to be playing at the elite highest level of your game and being able to win things. Now we played with certain players that had their opinions."

"Famously, Roy [Keane] was very outspoken, said a lot of things, but his level of performance at the time when he was saying these things, whether it's right or wrong, that's another argument. But his level of performance week in week out was there. You know, one of the best in Europe."

Butt went on to insist that Martinez is not playing at a level required for United, adding: "Now, it's still not right talking out. You can't do that, and punishments come. However, I think with Martinez, what he's basically saying is the players that I'm playing with aren't good enough."

"Now, you can't say that when you're in changing rooms. I don't think you can say that, and even more so when you're playing at a level that is not good enough for Man United. That's no disrespect to Martinez. It's just the way it is at the minute."

United's squad reinforcement decisions in the January transfer window is likely to have a bearing on Martinez's future, even though previous reports suggest that the club is relaxed about the player's situation. For now, the Red Devils need the Argentine to regain his form and deliver on the pitch.

Tottenham Hotspur fans complaining about the scheduling of the upcoming north London derby appear to have forgotten what happened with the last one.

The Premier League announced the remaining fixture amendments for December on Monday, including Arsenal's games against Brentford , Tottenham Hotspur , Bournemouth , and Manchester United .

Arsenal will travel away to Brentford on Wednesday, December 2nd at 20:15 GMT, then play Spurs on Sunday, December 6th at 16:30. The Gunners will face Bournemouth on Sunday, December 13th at 14:00, before playing Manchester United on Sunday, December 20th at 16:30.

In the midweeks between those matches, Arsenal will play Real Madrid on Wednesday, December 9th, and they might be involved in the League Cup fifth round in the week commencing December 14th.

It's a packed schedule, but Tottenham Hotspur fans have been complaining on social media that they have it worse. Whilst Arsenal face Brentford on the Wednesday, Spurs are scheduled to play Fulham on the Thursday, giving them a day less to prepare for Sunday's derby match.

Of course, this overlooks a couple of key details. Most significantly, that Spurs solely have the Premier League to worry about.

Whilst Arsenal will have one eye on their following game against Real Madrid, Spurs have no European football. They also don't have any League Cup games filling their schedule before or after the derby.

So Spurs might have to rest a player or two against Fulham if they want them fresh for Arsenal, but their squad is hardly going to be on its last legs going into the game.

The Spurs fans complaining also must have short memories, as Arsenal had it far worse earlier this year.

Whilst Spurs had a 12-day break in the lead-up to February's derby, Arsenal played three matches in that time, and they had just four days to prepare for the trip to Tottenham.

Rather than making excuses, the Gunners won that match 4-1. Spurs fans clearly don't back their team to deal with their current 'adversity' in the same way.

articles.title: Liverpool re-ignite interest in former target, the deal could be on
articles.summary: Liverpool are one of the most well-known clubs in the world. And, while this is good for certain deals, for others, it can cause the price of players to sky...
articles.body:
Liverpool are one of the most well-known clubs in the world.

And, while this is good for certain deals, for others, it can cause the price of players to sky rocket.

For example, if any other club came in for Ismaila Sarr towards the end of the summer transfer window, there's no way that Crystal Palace would have been demanding around £80 million to let him to leave .

Thanks to the heightened prices that Liverpool are given, this makes a lot of deals hard for them to agree.

So, even though they're linked with many different players every season, only three or four moves ever get confirmed but, they often keep tabs on players they think could become even better.

And, that seems to be exactly what they've done with one midfielder.

Liverpool are interested in signing Johan Manzambi again

In the summer, it felt almost impossible for Liverpool's fanbase to go a day without their club being linked with a new player.

Obviously, this was because they finished fifth in the Premier League last term which was a massive fall from grace.

Because, just the season before, they'd won the Premier League title and were one of the world's best teams with Luis Enrique even saying that Liverpool were the toughest team that Paris Saint-Germain had faced all season.

However, for one reason or another, things just didn't click during the 2025-26 campaign which led to Arne Slot being sacked and many transfer rumours emerging.

One of the main areas that they need to upgrade is their midfield and, although many players were rumoured to be potential options, one of them has now re-emerged as an option for Liverpool.

"In recent internal meetings, the decision-makers at Anfield Road have consistently spoken favorably about Manzambi," 442 wrote .

"And according to information from 4-4-2.ch , they have decided to monitor the 20-time international throughout the entire season. Liverpool's scouting department is certainly not making a mistake with this move.

"Firstly, Manzambi is already in excellent form just a few weeks after joining what is arguably the best football league in the world.

"Secondly, there are persistent transfer rumors surrounding Alexis Mac Allister, who is reportedly a top target for Real Madrid.

"Manzambi is quickly justifying the gigantic €60 million transfer fee . The Swiss prodigy is well on his way to establishing himself as a star player in the Premier League. Liverpool will be able to assess this precisely in the future."

Johan Manzambi could be a good signing for Liverpool in the summer

One good thing about Manzambi is that, because Aston Villa bought him in the summer, when Liverpool were also interested in him , by the end of the current campaign, he'll already have a years worth of experience in the Premier League.

However, for Aston Villa this season, he's mainly been used as a number 10 which, at the moment, isn't exactly what Liverpool need.

Because, even though Florian Wirtz is performing nowhere near the standards expected of him , he's still young and is the Reds' third-most expensive signing ever.

So, as much as fans want him to get dropped, unless another team comes in to try and buy him from Liverpool, there's no way that he's being replaced.

But, in the past, Manzambi has been used as a number eight and a number six so, if the Reds want him, he would probably be able to fit into Iraola's double pivot.

Here's hoping that, if new players are signed in the future that they're as good, if not better than Manzambi.

articles.title: Evanilson recupera el 'no look de Firmino
articles.summary: Michael Laudrup puso de moda los pases mirando al tendido en LaLiga y Roberto Firmino quiso ir un paso más allá patentando los goles 'no look' (sin mirar a portería) en la Premier League.
articles.body: Michael Laudrup puso de moda los pases mirando al tendido en LaLiga y Roberto Firmino quiso ir un paso más allá patentando los goles 'no look' (sin mirar a portería) en la Premier League. Su legado está en buenas manos. Otro brasileño, Evanilson, ha cogido su testigo. El ex del Oporto, fichado en 2024 a cambio de 44,8 millones de euros, lideró la victoria del Bournemouth (2-0) sobre el Sunderland, la primera en Premier con Marco Rose -sustituto de Andoni Iraola- en el banquillo. Evanilson marcó la diferencia. Asistió a Marcus Tavernier en el 4' después de robarle la cartera a Danso, forzó la expulsión del propio Danso en el 17'... y marcó el definitivo 2-0 en el 48'. Fue entonces cuando resucitó el famoso 'no look' de Firmino. El brasileño interceptó una mala cesión de Omar Alderete, sorteó a Robin Roefs en el mano a mano y, cuando se disponía a marcar a puerta vacía, giró descaradamente la cara hacia la grada que tenía a la izquierda. Un bonito tributo para conmemorar su gol 100 como profesional. Este curso acumula tres, dos en Premier. Suma, además, cuatro asistencias en nueve partidos. “Siempre es bastante bueno, pero diría que estuvo excepcional. Es uno de esos jugadores que nunca recibe el reconocimiento que merece a menos que marque. Me alegro mucho por él, porque ahora se ve recompensado con goles, ya que es un número nueve, un nueve y medio, a veces incluso jugó de diez esta temporada, y siempre trabaja duro para el equipo, tanto con el balón como sin él", aseguraba Marco Rose. “Mantiene la posesión, baja a recibir, presiona. Su esfuerzo es realmente excepcional. “Y sí, cuando baja, si juega un poco más atrás, sigue siendo un jugador muy bueno. Con sus habilidades técnicas, puede aportarnos mucho”, subraya el técnico del Bournemouth. El 'no look' ha vuelto a la Premier.

articles.title: Bengals progress report: Grading special teams
articles.summary: What grade do you think the Bengals’ special teams deserves at the bye?
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals are 3-2 coming out of their bye week, and depending on which side of the bed you wake up on, there's plenty of reason for optimism or pessimism.

The offense has had its moments. The defense has had its moments. Unfortunately, so have the special teams, and not necessarily in a good way.

Outside of Evan McPherson, who apparently decided missing field goals is for lesser mortals, Darrin Simmons' special teams units have been a frustrating combination of mediocrity and outright disaster.

Let's start with the one guy who's been keeping the lights on.

With 11 guys on the field working together, every play has a lot of moving pieces, but the field-goal unit is fairly simple. As long as the long snapper, holder, and kicker do their jobs, everyone else just needs to keep the defense out of the way for a second or two.

Outside of a penalty that pushed the Bengals out of field-goal range, Evan McPherson and the rest of the field-goal unit have been perfect.

McPherson now owns the franchise record for most consecutive field goals made with 22, a streak that stretches back to the 2025 season. In 2026, McPherson is a perfect 10-for-10. What's most impressive, though, is that five of those kicks have come from 50 or more yards, with a long of 58.

Obviously, the offense wants to walk away from every drive with seven points, but that's not always possible. The Bengals are extremely fortunate to have a kicker who is so accurate from beyond 50 yards. Nobody really cares about the kicker until a field goal can win or lose the game in the final minutes.

On the defensive side of things, the only major issue so far this season came in Week 5. Dexter Lawrence was flagged for roughing the snapper against the Dolphins, giving Miami a fresh set of downs after a successful field goal. The Dolphins eventually scored a touchdown, turning three points into seven.

The Bengals won that game, but those four additional points helped keep Miami within striking distance late in the fourth quarter.

Field Goal Unit: 98% (A+) Field Goal Block Unit: 85% (B) Overall Field Goal Unit: 92% (A-)

As far as punt coverage goes, the first major mistake came in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals' defense stopped Pittsburgh in the third quarter and forced a punt, but Cedric Johnson was called for an obvious roughing-the-kicker penalty. That gave the Steelers a fresh set of downs, and what should have been a defensive stop turned into a Pittsburgh touchdown a few plays later.

In the same game, former punt returner Ke'Shawn Williams muffed a punt that Pittsburgh recovered at the Bengals' 14-yard line. The defense managed to hold the Steelers to a field goal, but instead of Cincinnati getting the ball back with an opportunity to score, Pittsburgh walked away with three points.

Those two mistakes handed the Steelers possessions that resulted in 10 points in a game the Bengals lost by three.

Ryan Rehkow's punting, meanwhile, has been unspectacular. His 44.9 yards-per-punt average ranks among the lowest in the NFL. Nine of his 16 punts have been downed inside the 20-yard line, and he hasn't recorded a touchback.

There haven't been any major mistakes on Rehkow's part, but his overall production has been below average.

The real issue with this unit isn't necessarily the punter. It's the mistakes being made around him. A roughing penalty and a muffed punt aren't just bad plays. They're the kinds of mistakes that can cost a team a game, and against Pittsburgh, they helped do exactly that.

Punting Unit: 74% (C) Punt Return Unit: 49% (F) Overall Punting grade: 61 (D-)

Kickoffs are so different now than they used to be. With touchbacks generally bringing the ball out to the 35-yard line, teams have more incentive to kick short of the end zone and force a return. That means more opportunities for explosive plays, but it also means more opportunities for mistakes.

For the Bengals, the most glaring mistake came in Week 5 against the Dolphins.

Rookie wide receiver Dohnte Meyers fielded a kickoff at the four-yard line, but his momentum carried him out of bounds almost immediately, setting Joe Burrow and the offense up in the shadow of their own goalposts.

The offense managed to move the ball out near midfield, but the drive ultimately ended with a punt. While the mistake didn't directly cost Cincinnati points, it put the offense in a difficult position and eliminated any chance of starting that possession with favorable field position.

To be fair, Meyers also started that game with an 81-yard kickoff return that set the Bengals up at Miami's 10-yard line. Burrow and the offense took advantage, scoring a touchdown just three plays later.

That's the frustrating thing about the kickoff return unit. There's clearly potential for big plays, but the execution hasn't always been consistent.

On the coverage side, the Bengals haven't suffered any major breakdowns comparable to what we've seen from the punt units. They've generally done a respectable job of limiting opposing returners and avoiding the kind of disastrous plays that can completely flip field position.

Kickoff Unit Grade: 82% (B-) Kickoff Return Unit Grade: 79% (C+) Overall Kickoff/Return Grade: 80% (B -)

Darrin Simmons has been the Bengals' special teams coordinator since 2003. He was named assistant head coach in 2020 and has held both positions ever since. Special teams typically haven't been a major problem for the Bengals under Simmons, but this season has been different. Outside of McPherson, the unit has made several costly mistakes, and some have had a direct impact on the outcome of games.

The Bengals lost that game by three points, and two special teams mistakes gave the Steelers possessions that resulted in 10 points. It's impossible to say with certainty how the game would have unfolded without those errors, but it's hard not to wonder what Cincinnati's record would look like if those mistakes hadn't happened.

It's not all on Simmons. Players have to execute, and there are only so many things a coach can control once the ball is snapped. However, Simmons is responsible for preparing his units, and right now, those units aren't consistently getting the job done.

A 4-1 record, including a 1-0 start in the division, would sound a hell of a lot better than 3-2.

Hopefully, the Bengals got things straightened out during the bye week. Because without McPherson's excellence, Cincinnati's special teams would be earning a solid D.

articles.summary: El central francés dijo que "no hemos tenido mucha suerte al principio de temporada. Es cierto que he leído el tema de Negreira, pero estoy aquí para jugar al fútbol
articles.body: Konaté compareció por vez primera en rueda de prensa y dejó claro que conoce el caso Negreira y que "no hemos tenido mucha suerte al principio de temporada. Es cierto que he leído el tema de Negreira, pero estoy aquí para jugar al fútbol". El nombre de Konaté había acaparado la actualidad tras la acción del segundo gol del Real Madrid en la que el Sevilla reclamó falta del central madridista al delantero sevillista. Acción contra el Sevilla con Ure: "No he visto esos comentarios. ¿Viste la acción? Si para ti no es falta... No voy a decir que es falta, para mí es evidente". Sobre los arbitrajes al Real Madrid en esta temporada no se calló: "No hemos tenido mucha suerte al principio de temporada. Es cierto que he leído el tema de Negreira, pero estoy aquí para jugar al fútbol. Todos los que trabajamos para este club debemos pensar en eso. Yo intento ser competitivo y conseguir resultados. articles.summary: El francés fue el jugador que atendió a los medios en la previa del partido contra el Leipzig
articles.body: Vuelve la Champions al Bernabéu. El Madrid se enfrenta mañana al RB Leipzig tras la épica remontada lograda en Roma. Ibrahima Konaté fue el elegido para representar al vestuario en sala de prensa. Partido contra el Leipzig: "Es un partido especial para mí porque voy a jugar contra mi antiguo club. Estoy contento de ver a mis excompañeros. Sería bueno ganar mañana y ganar tres de tres para estar entre los primeros ocho. Tenemos una buena oportunidad". Primeras semanas en el Madrid y adaptación: "Está siendo increíble. Todo el mundo me está ayudando muchísimo, no he tenido problema con mi adaptación. Todo el mundo me está haciendo sentir muy bien. Lo más importante es conseguir títulos porque el nivel es muy alto". Polémica con la camiseta de Ceuta: "Para ser honestos, no entendí muy bien qué ponía en la camiseta. No hablaré de ese tema ahora. Después me enteré de lo que pasó en Ceuta y puedo entender ambas partes. Mis padres son de África y creo que hay mucha gente en esa situación. Hay una parte de la historia con la que podamos estar de acuerdo y otra no. No hay que hacer malas cosas en el país. No sabía a qué se refería y no supe qué hacer. Tengo que estar centrado en el fútbol, vine aquí para jugar al fútbol. No fue tan importante como se comentó". ¿El Madrid es lo que imaginaba?: "Es más de lo que esperaba, sinceramente. Los medios, todo se magnifica mucho más. Se habla de nosotros en todo el mundo. Estoy muy contento, siempre soñé con jugar en este club. Para mí es el mejor del mundo. No estoy muy metido en las redes sociales y no pienso en lo que dice la gente de nosotros. Podemos leer de todo". Arbitraje al Madrid: "No hemos tenido mucha suerte al principio de temporada. Es cierto que he leído el tema de Negreira, pero estoy aquí para jugar al fútbol. Todos los que trabajamos para este club debemos pensar en eso. Yo intento ser competitivo y conseguir resultados. Pero sí, no hemos tenido buena suerte en las decisiones de los árbitros". Diomande: "Tiene un talento muy bueno. Solo tiene 19 años y ya es increíble. Trabaja muy duro en el día a día. No puedo pensar por qué no va a triunfar en este equipo. Es una gran persona y estoy muy contento por sus últimos partidos". Acción contra el Sevilla con Ure: "No he visto esos comentarios. ¿Viste la acción? Si para ti no es falta... No voy a decir que es falta, para mí es evidente". Concentración teniendo el Clásico: "Es muy importante que nos concentremos siempre en el próximo partido. Si ganamos mañana, nos ayudará para el Clásico. Si nos centramos en el Clásico, no llegaremos en buen momento. Lo primero es mañana porque queremos ganar la Champions". Ancelotti decía que había defensas pesimistas y optimistas, ¿cómo se define usted?: "Soy un defensa optimista, sinceramente". Franceses en el vestuario: "Tuve suerte de compartir vestuario. Tchouaméni y Mbappé me hablaron mucho del club. Es positivo, aunque a veces puede ser negativo porque estamos un poco locos entre nosotros. Estoy contento de estar con ellos. Son grandes personas. También que Mendy vuelva pronto, le necesitamos".

articles.title: Mourinho talks Vinicius, Guler, Valverde, Mbappe, Espi, Diomande ahead of Real Madrid vs RB Leipzig
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho has made it clear that reputation alone will not guarantee a starting place at Real Madrid, with Vinicius Jr. facing the same performance deman...
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho has made it clear that reputation alone will not guarantee a starting place at Real Madrid, with Vinicius Jr. facing the same performance demands as the rest of the squad ahead of their Champions League meeting with RB Leipzig .

The Portuguese manager addressed several key issues during his pre-match press conference, discussing Real Madrid's European ambitions, the competition for places, his midfield options and the possibility of pairing Kylian Mbappe with Carlos Espi.

Mourinho makes Vinicius stance clear before Leipzig test

Asked whether Vinicius could lose his place in the starting line-up, Mourinho rejected the idea that any player should be guaranteed selection regardless of their performances.

"No one is untouchable. I don't like this concept of an 'untouchable' player. What makes a player untouchable is their performance on the pitch."

However, Mourinho confirmed that Vinicius would start on the left wing against Leipzig, leaving Yan Diomande uncertain about his involvement.

"Vinicius will play on the left wing tomorrow. Yan [Diomande] doesn't know whether he'll play tomorrow or not, so you can imagine."

The manager also highlighted the importance of professionalism within the squad, pointing to Jude Bellingham's recovery habits and Diomande's regular visits to the physiotherapist.

"In a positive sense, I like it when people say that. But it's also true: Jude has this culture of recovery and taking meticulous care of himself.

Mourinho confirms Vinicius Jr. will start against Leipzig. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

"Diomande always comes in the afternoon to see the physio. The most important thing is that there's an overall work ethic. No one stays here without one of my assistants being present."

Real Madrid focus on Champions League qualification

Despite Real Madrid's recent run of three consecutive victories, Mourinho insisted that it was too early to discuss the club's chances of winning the Champions League.

"It's far too early to say. Our aim right now is to qualify, and then the next objective will be to avoid the play-offs. I have a feeling we'll need a lot of points to do that.

"First, we need to reach the 11 or 12 points required to qualify, and then secure the points that will see us finish in the top eight."

Mourinho also praised the team's recent performances and called for similar consistency against Leipzig, while acknowledging that Madrid still have significant room for improvement.

"We've been here for three or four months; it's impossible to be where we want to be. We always have to improve, whether individually or as a team.

"I understand that the club's expectations are extremely high. I've been here for three years and I know exactly what they're like. I know there's a lot of work to be done."

He also expressed satisfaction with the appointment of an experienced referee for such an important fixture, describing the official as someone who would not tolerate unnecessary complaints.

Mourinho's Real Madrid are slowly building momentum. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

"Tomorrow we've got a referee who won't put up with any nonsense. He's of the very highest calibre and I'm really pleased to have a referee like that for such an important match."

Mourinho weighs midfield options and Mbappe partnership

Mourinho explained that Arda Guler and Federico Valverde offer different qualities but can adapt to multiple positions, with his selection decisions shaped by the opposition and the team's needs.

"They are different players, but both have the ability to adapt to different positions. Every match and every team is different. The other day we played with a different midfield.

"I try to put together the best line-up for the team. There's a time and place for everything, and I try to get things right. Sometimes I'll be right, and sometimes I won't."

The manager was less certain about combining Mbappe and Espi, suggesting that their partnership could create tactical difficulties depending on the formation and the wide players selected.

"It's difficult. It's possible for both of them to play in a 4-4-2, but with the wingers we have, it would be a 4-2-4. Timing is another matter, as happened in Rome."

Mourinho concluded by explaining that he had arrived at Madrid with a clear understanding of the club's expectations and remained focused on giving his best every day, rather than setting a predetermined timeline for his tenure.

"I didn't come here thinking I'd be here for 100 days or three years. I try to give my all every day," he concluded.

articles.title: 2 injured Arsenal players return to training pre-Bayern clash
articles.summary: Piero Hincapie and Kepa Arrizabalaga both took part in training on Tuesday morning, as Arsenal prepare to face Bayern Munich in the Champions League.Photo by...
articles.body:
Piero Hincapie and Kepa Arrizabalaga both took part in training on Tuesday morning, as Arsenal prepare to face Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

Arsenal received some good news on Tuesday morning, with injured duo Piero Hincapie and Kepa Arrizabalaga both taking part in training.

The Gunners were holding an open training session in front of the media, as is standard on the day before a Champions League match, allowing some insight into the fitness of the team's key players.

But though Hincapie was out on the grass training, he was only doing individual work on this occasion. It doesn't look as though he'll be ready for Wednesday's big game away to Bayern Munich , with the previous assessment of his injury suggesting he'd face another week or so out.

As for Kepa, the goalkeeper had only missed Sunday's game against Nottingham Forest with a knock, so if he's already back in training, he should be fit to make the squad against Bayern.

David Raya is obviously the more likely goalkeeper to start, but Champions League squads generally contain three goalkeepers, so there's space for both Kepa and Illan Meslier on the bench.

There was never any hope that Arsenal's other two injury absentees would be able to feature in this one, with Christos Tzolis and William Saliba not expected back this month.

Saliba has recently returned to training on the grass, but like Hincapie, he's only taking part in individual sessions at this stage.

The French international will need to rejoin full training before he has any chance to feature in a matchday squad, and he'll probably need some time to get back up to speed with his teammates on the training pitches.

Eight key first-team players did not train with the rest of the Manchester United group on Tuesday morning ahead of the trip to Como.

United are set to travel to Italy to face Cesc Fabregas' Como on Wednesday in just their third Champions League group match.

The Red Devils won their opener against Sabah FK before being beaten 2-0 by last season's semi-finalists, Atletico Madrid, at the Wanda Metropolitano last week. With United faltering in the Premier League, the Champions League can offer some respite, and Carrick will be eager for a convincing victory.

Steven Railston notes that Marcus Rashford, Lisandro Martinez, Ayden Heaven, Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw were all not part of the group that trained at Carrington today.

Mainoo missed the last two games against Atletico and Leeds with a minor issue. Shaw has already been sidelined twice this term , with his last appearance coming two weeks ago against Tottenham Hotspur. Martinez started in the 1-1 draw with Leeds but was taken off during the interval after sustaining a knock.

Rashford has been dealing with a hip problem, which United have been managing carefully. Meanwhile, Heaven was left out of the Leeds game due to illness.

Railston notes, "United sources have confirmed a decision will be made on each of the aforementioned players' involvement against Como. Some could still make the travelling squad to Italy after a late check today, but it appears unlikely, which would mean Carrick's defensive options could be depleted."

"Leny Yoro was another absentee on Tuesday morning, but he received a red card against Atletico, meaning he is suspended for the Como game. Yoro is set to complete full training, while the main group took part in a light session ahead of their flight to Italy."

Goalkeepers: Lammens, Darlow, Heaton, Mee. Defenders: Maguire, De Ligt, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Kamason.

articles.title: What does Celtic's demolition of Hearts mean for Kasper Hogh?
articles.summary: BBC Scotland examines whether Celtic’s 7-1 win over Hearts proved they are better without their record signing.
articles.body:
Celtic's mauling of Hearts eliminated many of the question marks hanging over Martin O'Neill's side - but one significant question remains.

What does Sunday's incredible seven-goal victory tell us about record signing Kasper Hogh's place in the team?

Benched for the visit of last season's Scottish Premiership runners-up, a dynamic front three of Camilo Duran, Callum Osmand and Haissem Hassan were integral to a scintillating attacking display.

In the aftermath of last Thursday's chastening Europa League defeat at Benfica, during which Hogh was hooked at half-time, O'Neill backed the 25-year-old to end the campaign with 20 goals.

But is the £11m man now fighting for a starting spot?

Jota 'met some demons' during long injury absence

'Four points is nothing' - O'Neill stays cool after statement win

Celtic score seven in humiliation of title rivals Hearts

Having scored in just one of his 12 Celtic appearances - a hat-trick at Kilmarnock in August - O'Neill acknowledges his marquee summer acquisition is low on confidence, with a Europa League match against Celta Vigo to come on Thursday.

"He has lost a bit of confidence, but we will get that back during the course of time," the veteran boss said in the lead-up to Sunday's demolition of Hearts.

"We have game after game after game between now and January, but he will score goals for us, there is no question about it, and it is just a matter of tinkering around, but that's the nature of the business."

The Denmark forward did come off the bench at the weekend to set up Benjamin Nygren for Celtic's seventh goal. He also assisted the Sweden midfielder during the 2-0 win at Motherwell seven days earlier.

However, Hogh's performance in the 4-1 defeat in Lisbon, sandwiched between those two Premiership victories, intensified the debate surrounding his place in the team.

"If I'm a creative player and I've got Duran and Hogh to pick from, I'm taking Duran every day of the week," former Celtic midfielder Scott Allan said.

"He looks to get off the side of defenders. If you put a ball into the area, he's more likely to be alive to it."

Hogh was brought off at the break in Lisbon, with Duran, who has been the standout of Celtic's summer arrivals, moved to the centre of the attack.

With Hassan and Osmand on either side, O'Neill's frontline looked far more potent in a much-improved second-half display.

The same trio that finished Thursday's match started on Sunday, and Hearts simply could not live with them.

An Osmand double helped the champions establish a 5-1 half-time lead, while Duran's ninth goal of the campaign was one of two Celtic goals after the break.

Listen to live match commentary on BBC Sounds and follow text updates on the BBC Sport website and app.

'Celtic's best attack doesn't include Hogh'

It seems inconceivable that an £11m signing would not be a guaranteed starter for a Scottish club.

That said, Celtic fans were encouraged to see Hogh embrace fellow forward Osmand as he left the pitch at half-time on Sunday.

There is therefore nothing to suggest, from the outside, that ego will get in the way if the Dane spends time out of the first-choice XI.

Sunday's emphatic 7-1 victory has gone some way towards settling the debate, at least for now: Celtic's best forward line appears to be one that does not include their record signing.

"There have been question marks over whether Celtic's best attack involves Hogh. For me, it doesn't," BBC Scotland pundit Andy Halliday said on The Monday Night Club .

The former Hearts, Rangers and Motherwell midfielder added: "There's no doubt there's a goalscorer in there with Hogh. You don't score in the Champions League against Manchester City, Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid if you're not. He's just a goalscorer who isn't scoring goals."

The same cannot be said of Duran, who is thriving in a Celtic shirt and has 14 goal contributions - nine goals and five assists - in 15 games, many of which have come while playing in a wide role.

However, O'Neill has said that the Colombia international prefers to play centrally, and Halliday believes he can offer Celtic much more in that position - but what does that mean for Hogh?

"You look at Duran as a number nine on Sunday, the part he plays in the third goal, the fourth goal," Halliday said.

"When Jamie McCart takes a loose touch, Hogh wouldn't be close enough or quick enough to get on to that loose ball and spring Celtic into attack. Duran isn't just a goalscorer, he's so much more than that - and you saw that on Sunday.

"O'Neill still reckons Hogh will score 20 goals this season. It's hard to suggest he wouldn't, given his previous record at Bodo/Glimt, but at this moment in time, he isn't doing enough to be in Celtic's attack.

"O'Neill's searching for his best team and best front three, and the three you saw on Sunday are that."

articles.title: Mourinho: "Lo que hace intocables a los jugadores es su nivel en el campo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico atendió a los medios en la rueda de prensa previa al partido ante el Leipzig
articles.summary: El técnico atendió a los medios en la rueda de prensa previa al partido ante el Leipzig
articles.body: El Real Madrid regresa a su competición fetiche tras la remontada épica lograda en Roma. Lo hará en casa y ante el RB Leipzig de Demichelis. En la previa, José Mourinho atendió a los medios en una rueda de prensa en la que evitó el ruido del arbitraje y dejó claro que lo único intocable "es el escudo". Partido de mañana: "El Leipzig es el equipo que ha ganado al PSV, tiene tres puntos y se quiere clasificar. Nosotros ganamos tres partidos en poco tiempo y el último ganamos jugando muy bien. Hay que seguir. No por ganar tres, ganas el cuarto". ¿Le dirá a sus jugadores que se pueden pedir revisiones de VAR?: "El árbitro de mañana no está para bromas. La personalidad que tiene no hará que el VAR tenga tanta importancia. Estoy contento con Kovacs". Favoritos a la Champions: "No, es pronto. El Madrid no tiene objetivo de ganar la Champions, ahora es el de clasificarse. Si después llegamos a los puntos, veremos el segundo objetivo, que es evitar el playoff. Eso se puede evitar. Van a ser necesarios muchos puntos para escapar del playoff. Vamos poco a poco. Primero llegar a estar entre los 11/12, y después ir con todo para ganar". Gran presencia de sus jugadores y staff en Valdebebas: "Yo me he quedado esta noche. Las horas que estás aquí no significan que estás trabajando. Puede que un jugador escape escondido en un coche y vosotros no lo sabéis. En el sentido positivo, me gusta que se diga. Jude tiene esa cultura de recuperar y cuidar los detalles. Diomande viene siempre por la tarde con el fisio para cuidarse mucho. Lo más importante es que hay una dinámica normal aquí dentro. Me gusta mucho". Vinicius y Diomande: "Intocable es el escudo. Lo que hace intocables a los jugadores no es el brazalete, el estatus o los años que lleven, es su nivel en el campo". Nivel del equipo: "Falta mucho. Estamos aquí desde hace 3 meses. Imposible estar donde queremos. Hay que mejorar siempre colectivamente. Cuanto más conocimiento tenemos, más empatía tenemos. Las exigencias son máximas. Me hacen perfectamente consciente, pero no podemos perder la dirección de que hay mucho trabajo por hacer a diferentes niveles. Por ejemplo, el aspecto táctico es una acumulación de conocimiento. Yo no soy un entrenador cabezón de los que vive o muere con una idea. Eso significa que estoy siempre abierto a analizar y entender cosas para buscar lo mejor". Güler y Valverde: "Lo mejor para ellos es estar en el campo. Son diferentes y tienen experiencia diferente. Tienen esa capacidad de ser multifuncional y adaptarse a varias posiciones. Hay jugadores que si no juegan en su posición, no juegan. No es algo que se pueda elegir. El otro día jugamos con un centro del campo diferente, con uno más posicional y otro más de creación. Depende de la situación. Yo intento hacer la mejor combinación posible para dar equilibrio y calidad. Si hubiéramos jugado en Roma con Bernardo y Arda desde inicio, nos meten cinco porque no teníamos la capacidad para soportar. Alguna vez tendré razón, otras no". ¿Espí y Mbappé son compatibles?: "Es difícil. Al inicio, difícil. Con un 4-4-2, sí, pero con ese esquema los jugadores de banda es un 4-2-4, y ahí tengo dudas de que ganemos". Fran Soto dice que los árbitros españoles son los mejores del mundo: "Para mí, mis jugadores son los mejores del mundo. Entiendo que él diga que sus árbitros son los mejores del mundo". Balance de sus primeros 100 días: "Estaba preparado. No puedo hablar de sorpresas ni de si me lo esperaba mejor o peor. Me esperaba lo que me he encontrado. He querido ver con mis ojos y también escuchar. No he venido pensando que voy a estar 100 días o tres años. Intento dar lo máximo cada día". Rol de Diomande mañana: "Mañana va a jugar Vinicius de extremo izquierdo. Yan no sabe si va a jugar mañana o no, así que imagínate".

articles.title: Bayern Munich star Jonathan Tah understands the big challenge Arsenal will present
articles.summary: FC Bayern vs. Arsenal will be a hige match/.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich defender Jonathan Tah knows that Wednesday's Champions League showdown against Arsenal will be a serious test, and he has plenty of respect for what Mikel Arteta has built in North London.

Speaking to The Times journalist Jonathan Northcroft (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Tah praised Arsenal's recent progress, highlighting the team's identity and the difficulty of facing them on the pitch.

"Arsenal have been doing great the last years, the way they build this team and this identity. We faced them last year and felt how difficult it was to play against them. And it's always more interesting if a team has a player you know and want to support," Tah said.

Tah, of course, was referencing his old pal from his playing days at Bayer Leverkusen, Kai Havertz. The German international knows firsthand how challenging Arsenal can be, with Bayern having experienced their quality in last season's Champions League campaign. Arsenal have developed into one of Europe's most formidable sides under Arteta, combining defensive organization with an increasingly dangerous attacking game.

For Bayern Munich, Wednesday's meeting represents another opportunity to measure themselves against elite European opposition. Vincent Kompany's side will need to be sharp in possession, disciplined defensively, and clinical in front of goal if they want to leave London with a positive result.

Tah's final comment also adds an interesting personal angle to the matchup. Having faced familiar opponents and developed relationships throughout his career, the Bayern defender clearly appreciates the extra motivation that comes with competing against someone he knows and wants to support.

However, sentiment will only go so far once the whistle blows. Bayern Munich will have to put that respect aside and deliver a top-level performance against an Arsenal side that has plenty of reasons to believe it can compete for the biggest prizes in Europe.

articles.title: Vote for Blue FCU's Fort Collins-area Football Player of Week (Week 8)
articles.summary: Vote for your Blue FCU Fort Collins-area Football Player of the Week, with nominees from Fort Collins, Fossil Ridge, Wellington and Windsor.
articles.body:
The Coloradoan is proud to present another aspect of our weekly Athlete of the Week series, partnering with Blue Federal Credit Union to honor the best Fort Collins-area tackle football players throughout the fall 2026 season.

The weekly Fort Collins-area Football Player of the Week poll has five nominees, and fans can vote every Tuesday through Thursday at coloradoan.com/sports .

You can find the nominees and the ballot below. Voting is open this week until 11:59 p.m. on Oct. 22, now closed this week , with the winner officially announced on Oct. 23.

Return to this page to see the official winner and a video of this week's Fort Collins-area Football Player of the Week. You can see last week's winner in the video currently atop this page.

Fans can nominate their favorite players (deadline: 11:59 p.m. every Sunday) and the Coloradoan sports staff will ultimately select the nominees each week.

If you have nominations for a future football Player of the Week, please send them via email to ChrisAbshire@coloradoan.com for consideration.

Meet Blue FCU Football Player of the Week nominees for Week 8 (Oct. 15-16)

Memphis Clause, Fossil Ridge DB: The SaberCat sophomore had a breakout game on the city rivalry stage, recording five tackles (three solo) and picking off Fort Collins QB Jace Garcia twice as part of a fantastic Fossil defensive performance that limited the Lambkins' high-octane offense to just 21 points.

Brayton Meglen, Wellington RB: It was another huge game for the Eagles junior star. Meglen carried the ball 20 times for 241 yards and five more touchdowns in a 55-22 win over University for his fourth game with at least four TDs in the last month.

Diego Romero, Fort Collins DB/RB: What a Senior Night performance for the Lambkins two-way standout. Romero had a team-high 110 all-purpose yards, made two tackles with two pass deflections and scored two of Fort Collins' three TDs, one a rushing touchdown and the other a pick-six interception return.

Vicente Romero, Fort Collins DB/RB: It was a similar story for the other Romero twin, who also excelled alongside his brother on Senior Night. Romero had seven tackles and a team-high 86 rushing yards, including a game-clinching fourth-quarter rushing touchdown.

Everett Wood, Windsor LB: Wood put in a yeoman's effort on defense despite the Wizards' loss to 3A No. 3 Holy Family. Wood record a game-high 11 tackles (six solo, one for loss) and recorded an interception against one of the state's top QB in Kaden Hopkin.

articles.title: Pellegrini: "La relación entre el árbitro y el VAR es lo que hay que mejorar"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Betis comparece en la previa del partido frente al Feyenoord
articles.summary: El técnico del Betis comparece en la previa del partido frente al Feyenoord
articles.body: El Feyenoord visita mañana (21.00 horas) al Betis en La Cartuja en la tercera jornada de la liguilla de la Champions League. Esta mañana ha tenido lugar el último entrenamiento con las ausencias de Cucho Hernández y Junior, y este mediodía han comparecido ante los medios Manuel Pellegrini y Pablo Fornals. El técnico espera "un partido complicado, jugamos de nuevo contra otro líder de su liga. Buscaremos el partido, pero tenemos las armas futbolísticas para tratar de ganar en casa". Pasa página. "Es algo que hablo habitualmente con los jugadores. Las 24 horas siguiente a una derrota o una victoria son para disfrutarlas cuando uno gana y para pasar la amargura cuando uno pierde. El marcador está hecho, lo que sucedió, sucedió, y solo pensamos en el partido de Champions de mañana y no en el partido de Liga". Rotaciones. "Para mí todos los jugadores son importantes. Jugando ocho partidos en 27 días hay que tener una dosificación, son muchos los variantes que uno analiza antes de hacer el once y estimamos el mejor equipo inicial ante el Barcelona y mañana haremos lo mismo. Que alguien no haya jugado el partido anterior no quiere decir que vaya a jugar el siguiente. Los cinco cambios después son tan importantes como los que inician". El VAR. "Nunca deja de ser una ayuda. La posibilidad de revisar una acción una segunda vez, pero la autoridad tiene que tenerla siempre el árbitro y esa relación árbitro-VAR es lo que hay que mejorar. Mantengo mi convicción de que el VAR ayuda muchísimo a cometer menos errores". Tiempo de revisión. "No sabía que había este programa. Una cosa es la prensa, tienen derecho a hacer todos los programas, y otra la realidad del fútbol, que es distinta. No creo que tenga gran influencia las palabras que uno dice, cada uno analizará eso con la objetividad que cada uno tenga que tener. No es un tema en el que esté pensando". Parrott. "Para mañana Troy seguro que es mejor que Cucho porque está lesionado y lo más probable es que juegue. Estamos muy conformes con el rendimiento de los dos jugadores, han hecho goles importantes, dos nueve que nos dan capacidad de juego en el área buena. Dentro de un plantel, más que comparar, lo importante es el rendimiento y nadie tendrá quejas de ninguno de los dos hasta el momento".
